terms.definition: The total force of particles colliding with the walls of the container, acting at right angles to the walls.
The temperature of a gas is related to the average kinetic energy of its particles.
Raising the temperature increases pressure, because particles collide with the walls more often and with more force.
For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure × volume = constant.
Doing work on a gas (such as pumping a tyre) increases its internal energy, so its temperature rises.
